St. Nektarios of Aegina

Saints

St. Nektarios of Aegina

St. Nectarius Kephalas · St. Anastasios Kephalas · St. Nektarios of Pentapolis

Period
1846–1920; officially recognized as a saint in 1961
Region
Thrace, Chios, Alexandria, Athens, Aegina
Titles / vocation
Bishop · Venerable · Wonderworker
Commemoration
November 9

Introduction

St. Nektarios of Aegina is remembered as bishop of Pentapolis, teacher, founder of a women’s monastery, and spiritual father who endured unjust accusation. His life joins education and pastoral responsibility with patient suffering.

Read the published life [1]

BackgroundLife and notable eventsDeath and martyrdomWritings and legacyChronology
Death / martyrdom

Died after illness and hospitalization in 1920; not executed

Read circumstances and sources

Background

The OCA recounts his childhood poverty and work in Constantinople. It preserves the story of a boy’s letter to Christ, a compassionate neighboring merchant, and his employer’s mistaken accusation of theft. These are named features of the church’s life.

[1] Published ecclesiastical life or account · Published life, selected article paragraphs 2, 4, 5, 6, 7, 8, 9

The parish biography follows his teaching on Chios, monastic life, studies at Athens, and service in Egypt. After university graduation in 1885, he is ordained priest and later consecrated metropolitan of Pentapolis in 1889. It emphasizes both preaching and administrative responsibility before his removal.

[2] Published ecclesiastical life or account · Published life, selected article paragraphs 33, 34, 35

Life and notable events

GOARCH’s educational account describes the accusations of 1890 as slander and presents his removal from Alexandria as an injustice. It distinguishes suspension from duties and exile from the later work he undertook in Greece. Its central theme is his refusal to nourish hatred toward his accusers. That interpretation belongs to the published church account, rather than an invented statement of his motives.

[3] Published ecclesiastical life or account · November 7, 2024, 1890 accusations and forgiveness

In Greece he preaches, directs the Rizarios school, and helps establish Holy Trinity Monastery on Aegina. The parish account describes writing, confession, gardening, carrying stones, and work on the buildings. It links practical labor with continued pastoral service.

[2] Published ecclesiastical life or account · Published life, selected article paragraphs 36, 37

This later educational account also places his service at Rizarios and the foundation on Aegina after his expulsion from Alexandria. It therefore does not make the accusation the end of his ministry. The continuity of teaching, care for a monastic community, and a willingness to forgive supplies the publication’s interpretation of his response to injustice.

[3] Published ecclesiastical life or account · November 7, 2024, 1890 accusations and forgiveness

Death and martyrdom

The selected accounts place his death in 1920 after hospitalization, rather than execution. The OCA and parish biographies print different November dates; this profile retains the year and the published November 9 commemoration without silently harmonizing the dates.

[1] Published ecclesiastical life or account · Published life, selected article paragraphs 24, 30

Writings and legacy

The parish account dates the uncovering of his relics to 1953 and recognition by the Ecumenical Patriarchate to 1961. It records the widespread veneration and healing traditions attached to his memory. Those reports remain attributed to the church publication.

[2] Published ecclesiastical life or account · Published life, selected article paragraphs 38, 39

The DRE account presents forgiveness as a defining feature of his witness after suffering false accusations. It relates that theme to his later teaching and the continuing devotion at Aegina. Miracle reports are reported as the publication’s ecclesiastical testimony, not as medical advice or guarantees.

[3] Published ecclesiastical life or account · November 7, 2024, 1890 accusations and forgiveness
